s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive bilateral nasal airway obstruction with highly vascularized mass
salient_findings: Voluminous, pulsatile, highly vascularized mass in both nasal cavities
Hypervascular tumor with anterior skull base extension
Considerable uptake on radioiodine scintigraphy regarding rib and vertebral lesions
key_facts: Woman in her 30s with no relevant medical history
Progressive bilateral nasal airway obstruction
Endoscopic examination found a voluminous, pulsatile, highly vascularized mass in both nasal cavities
CT scan showed a hypervascular tumor in the nasal cavity, on the left thyroid, the fifth rib, and the L4 vertebra
MRI confirmed a hypervascular tumor with anterior skull base extension
Radioiodine scintigraphy found considerable uptake regarding rib and vertebral lesions
Sinonasal tumor had low uptake on radioiodine scintigraphy
Serum thyroglobulin was significantly elevated at 4432 ng/mL
Biopsy results confirmed VTC metastasis in the costal and sinonasal tumor biopsies

shortlist.label: Papillary thyroid carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated serum thyroglobulin and biopsy results confirm VTC metastasis

shortlist.label: Follicular thyroid carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Highly vascularized mass and metastasis to distant sites are consistent with follicular thyroid carcinoma

shortlist.label: Medullary thyroid carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, medullary thyroid carcinoma can present with metastasis and elevated tumor markers

shortlist.label: Hürthle cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare type of thyroid cancer that can present with metastasis and vascularized masses

shortlist.label: Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive type of thyroid cancer that can present with rapid progression and metastasis

shortlist.label: Vertebral metastasis from thyroid cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Confirmed by biopsy results and imaging studies

shortlist.label: Esthesioneuroblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, esthesioneuroblastoma can present with nasal masses and metastasis

shortlist.label: Sinonasal undifferentiated carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare and aggressive type of cancer that can present with nasal masses and metastasis

raw.rationale: The presence of a highly vascularized and pulsatile mass in the nasal cavities, along with significantly elevated serum thyroglobulin and biopsy results confirming VTC metastasis, points towards a thyroid cancer metastasis. Papillary thyroid carcinoma is the most common type of thyroid cancer and can metastasize to distant sites, including the nasal cavity.

rejected.label: Follicular thyroid carcinoma
rejected.why: Less common than papillary thyroid carcinoma and less likely to metastasize to the nasal cavity

rejected.label: Medullary thyroid carcinoma
rejected.why: Typically has a different clinical presentation and is less likely to have high thyroglobulin levels

rejected.label: Hürthle cell carcinoma
rejected.why: A rare type of thyroid cancer, less likely to be the correct diagnosis

rejected.label: Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with a more aggressive clinical course and is less likely to have a long history of progressive symptoms

rejected.label: Vertebral metastasis from thyroid cancer
rejected.why: While the patient does have vertebral metastasis, the primary diagnosis is more likely to be a specific type of thyroid cancer rather than just a metastasis

rejected.label: Esthesioneuroblastoma
rejected.why: A rare tumor of the nasal cavity, but the presence of thyroid cancer metastasis is more likely given the clinical and laboratory findings

rejected.label: Sinonasal undifferentiated carcinoma
rejected.why: A rare and aggressive tumor, but the clinical and laboratory findings are more consistent with a metastasis from a thyroid cancer
